originalTitle: Ukraine war briefing: Pressure stays on Russian economy until war is over, says Bessent
summary: US treasury secretary speaks with Russian counterpart who is controversially attending G20 talks; India’s Modi says war must end. What we know on day 1,651
content: No economic relief for Russia is ‌possible ‌until its war in Ukraine ‌ends, the US treasury secretary, Scott Bessent, has told a Russian counterpart. Bessent met with Anton Siluanov, the Russian finance minister, at a G20 finance leaders’ meeting in Asheville, North Carolina, where Moscow’s representatives were a surprise and unwelcome presence. A source told Reuters that Bessent said no agreements of any kind were ‌possible ‌until the war ended. The Russian finance minister’s ⁠first in-person G20 appearance since Russia invaded Ukraine has irritated European officials ‌who are working on more sanctions against Russia. Britain on Monday ramped up pressure on ⁠shadow financial systems underpinning Russia’s war economy, doubling penalties for sanctions breaches, the UK treasury said. Fines would increase from 50% of the value of a sanctions breach to 100%, said John ⁠Healey, the UK finance minister. The UK’s National Crime Agency issued a nationwide ‌alert targeting the Kremlin-backed A7 network, which the British government has said was used to route funds and evade restrictions. Explosions were reported early on Tuesday morning in Kyiv, the Ukrainian capital. Four people ‌were injured, including two children, ‌and people should ‌seek shelter, local authorities said. Air raid alerts covered ‌most of Ukraine’s territory in the early hours of Tuesday. AFP said its correspondents in Kyiv saw flashes and heard loud explosions moments after Ukraine’s air force warned of inbound high-speed targets. It comes as Kyiv endures hours of daytime air raids and air raid warnings, Dan Sabbagh writes from the Ukrainian capital. Russia fired 800 jet-powered drones into Ukraine in the previous four days. Past versions of the Iranian-style Shahed drones were propeller-driven. In response, Ukrainian engineers are racing to make faster interceptor drones. “Four companies have developed the relevant interceptor drones, and one company has the most successful technology,” said Volodymyr Zelenskyy, Ukraine’s president. Nato ⁠fighter planes were scrambled, Latvia’s military said early on Tuesday, after ⁠a warning ‌of a ‌possible air ‌threat near the town of Ludza, close ‌to the Russian border. Separately, Russia’s north-western Leningrad region issued a drone ⁠threat alert, according to the governor, ‌Alexander Drozdenko. Ukrainian drones have hit another Wildberries warehouse, this time in Ekaterinburg, Russia. The Russian local governor confirmed the strike ‌on Monday, claiming that drones ‌and debris ‌also struck residential buildings. There were no casualties, he said. The suspected Russian “shadow fleet” oil tanker MV Sun was boarded ⁠by the ⁠European Union’s naval mission in the Mediterranean on Sunday, said Kaja Kallas, the EU’s ⁠foreign policy chief. “The oil ‌tanker MV Sun, suspected ‌of sailing under false flag in breach of international maritime law, was boarded on August 30 in the ‌Mediterranean by Operation Eunavfor Med Irini forces for flag verification,” Kallas posted. The war in Ukraine must end for humanity’s sake, India’s prime minister, Narendra Modi, told Vladimir Putin as the two met in Kyrgyzstan. “Every day that the war continues, humanity is, in effect, set back a step, whilst every step towards peace gives all of humanity real hope for peace,” Modi said. “We need to move from endless war to an end to the war, to a cessation of hostilities. And we will need to move precisely in this direction.” Despite international condemnation and sanctions, India, along with China, has remained one of the biggest buyers ‌of Russian oil, which has helped Moscow fund its war against Ukraine. Modi and the Russian president met on the sidelines of ‌the Shanghai Cooperation Organization summit where Putin ⁠and his Chinese counterpart, Xi ⁠Jinping, also met and briefly discussed ⁠the Ukraine war, the Kremlin said. Indonesia said it was investigating claims that several citizens had joined the Russian military to fight in the war in Ukraine. Information from Ukrainian authorities was being checked, the foreign ministry in Jakarta said. It did not say how many Indonesians were under suspicion, but they risk losing their citizenship. “If the involvement of Indonesian citizens in the armed forces of a foreign country is verified, it is an individual act and does not represent the policy or position of the Indonesian government,” the foreign ministry said. Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on Monday that he ⁠held a “detailed ⁠and constructive” call with US envoys ⁠Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner. Both sides were ⁠working to finalise dates for their visit ‌to Ukraine. “I ‌also informed them about the situation on the battlefield, where Russia’s gains have been sparse and at the cost of ‌huge losses, and about the strikes,” Zelenskyy said. “We shall see what the US president’s representatives manage to achieve. September ⁠could bring about a lot of changes. And we, together with our partners, must do ‌everything we can to protect people.” Polish prosecutors are investigating a fire at a drone factory as an act of terrorism arranged by a foreign intelligence service. The fire at the WB Electronics factory in the central city of Skarzysko-Kamienna was started deliberately using a “device containing flammable materials”, a prosecution statement said. Several countries in eastern Europe have said they have been the target of spying and sabotage as part of a “hybrid war” by Russia. Ukraine’s top sanctions official, Vladyslav Vlasiuk, will visit Washington this week to urge members of the US House ⁠of Representatives to approve sweeping ⁠Russia sanctions legislation. It would enable the president to sanction Russian officials and authorise tariffs on China, India and other countries for buying Russian oil and gas. Some US lawmakers and industries are wary, though, that Donald Trump might abuse the powers that the legislation contains. The House has not yet scheduled a vote on the legislation.
chineseTitle: 乌克兰战争简报：贝森特表示，在战争结束之前俄罗斯经济仍面临压力
chineseSummary: 美国财政部长与备受争议地参加 G20 峰会的俄罗斯财政部长通话；印度莫迪表示战争必须结束。第 1,651 天我们所知道的
chineseContent: 美国财政部长斯科特·贝森特对俄罗斯同行表示，在乌克兰战争结束之前，俄罗斯不可能获得经济救济。贝森特在北卡罗来纳州阿什维尔举行的二十国集团 (G20) 金融领导人会议上会见了俄罗斯财政部长安东·西卢安诺夫 (Anton Siluanov)，莫斯科代表的出席令人惊讶且不受欢迎。一位消息人士告诉路透社，贝森特表示，在战争结束之前不可能达成任何形式的协议。自俄罗斯入侵乌克兰以来，俄罗斯财长首次亲自出席 G20 峰会，这激怒了正在对俄罗斯实施更多制裁的欧洲官员。英国财政部表示，英国周一加大了对支撑俄罗斯战时经济的影子金融体系的压力，将违反制裁的处罚加倍。英国财政部长约翰·希利 (John Healey) 表示，罚款将从违反制裁金额的 50% 增加到 100%。英国国家犯罪局针对克里姆林宫支持的 A7 网络发布了全国范围的警报，英国政府表示该网络被用来转移资金和逃避限制。据报道，乌克兰首都基辅周二凌晨发生爆炸。地方当局表示，四人受伤，其中包括两名儿童，人们应该寻求庇护。周二凌晨，空袭警报覆盖了乌克兰大部分领土。法新社称，在乌克兰空军警告高速目标袭来后不久，驻基辅的记者看到了闪光并听到了巨大的爆炸声。丹·萨巴格在乌克兰首都写道，此时基辅正在忍受数小时的白天空袭和空袭警报。过去四天内，俄罗斯向乌克兰发射了 800 架喷气式无人机。过去版本的伊朗式“沙赫德”无人机是螺旋桨驱动的。作为回应，
